projectName: Bitcoin Accounting Rebrand and Compatibility Migration
description: Migrate project identity and code-level naming from cryptoAccounting/CryptoAccounts to bitcoinAccounting/BitcoinAccounts across runtime modules, entrypoints, tests, package metadata, and documentation, while preserving backward compatibility for existing users and automation.

rolloutContext.implication: Use compatibility-first rollout now, then clean up legacy names after public launch stabilization.

principles: Backward Compatibility First - Existing imports, CLI commands, and module entrypoints continue to work during migration
Safe Defaults and Data Continuity - New default paths prefer ~/.bitcoinaccounting with transparent fallback to existing ~/.cryptoaccounting locations
Incremental Refactor - Deliver rename work in staged stories with clear verification gates
Bitcoin-First Language - Product copy and UX prioritize Bitcoin and fiat-to-Bitcoin workflows without breaking multi-asset internals
Defer Breaking Changes - Hard removals of legacy names happen in a later cleanup feature after deprecation period

stages.name: Compatibility Foundation
stages.goal: Introduce bitcoin* canonical modules and class aliases while keeping legacy crypto* imports operational.

stages.name: Adoption Across Codebase
stages.goal: Move internal imports, scripts, tests, and packaging to bitcoin* canonical names.

stages.name: UX, Docs, and Path Migration
stages.goal: Complete user-facing rebrand, update default directories, and document migration/deprecation policy.

userStories.title: Add canonical bitcoin modules with legacy shims
acceptanceCriteria: Create canonical modules: src/python/bitcoinAccounts.py and src/python/bitcoinAccounting.py
Define canonical class name BitcoinAccounts and preserve CryptoAccounts as alias for compatibility
Retain legacy modules src/python/cryptoAccounts.py and src/python/cryptoAccounting.py as compatibility shims forwarding to canonical modules
Top-level module launcher remains operational for both python -m cryptoAccounting and python -m bitcoinAccounting
Add lightweight deprecation warnings in legacy entrypoints/import paths (non-fatal)

userStories.title: Migrate internal imports and type references to bitcoin canonical names
acceptanceCriteria: All src/python and src/scripts imports use bitcoinAccounts/BitcoinAccounts as canonical path/type
TYPE_CHECKING imports in TUI screens and scripts updated to canonical naming
Legacy imports remain accepted via shims for third-party or user scripts

userStories.title: Update package metadata and console entrypoints
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml py-modules include canonical bitcoin modules
Console script bitcoin-accounting resolves to canonical bitcoinAccounting:main
Legacy console scripts (crypto-accounting, crypto-tui) remain available and forward to canonical entrypoint
Project description updated to Bitcoin-first wording without changing backend capabilities
userStories.testStrategy: python -m pip install -e . && python -m bitcoinAccounting && python -m cryptoAccounting

userStories.title: Migrate default local data/cache paths with fallback
acceptanceCriteria: Default SQLite path becomes ~/.bitcoinaccounting/ledger.db when SQLITE_DB_PATH is unset
If ~/.bitcoinaccounting path does not exist but ~/.cryptoaccounting data exists, application can still read legacy location safely (documented precedence)
Default cache path for visualization/data fetcher becomes ~/.bitcoinaccounting/cache
Migration behavior covered by tests for path resolution and cache directory defaults

userStories.title: Rebrand TUI and user-facing strings to Bitcoin Accounting
acceptanceCriteria: TUI app title, help text, splash/menu copy, and theme comments updated from Crypto Accounting to Bitcoin Accounting
Product copy emphasizes Bitcoin-first accounting and fiat swapping where relevant
Tests asserting UI strings updated accordingly

userStories.title: Update documentation and migration guidance
acceptanceCriteria: README.md, GETTING_STARTED.md, .env.example, and script docs use bitcoinAccounting naming and ~/.bitcoinaccounting defaults
Add explicit migration section: old command/module/path compatibility and recommended updates
Clarify deprecation window for legacy crypto* names and when removal will occur
userStories.testStrategy: Manual documentation review + smoke run of documented commands

userStories.title: Planning and governance updates
acceptanceCriteria: Add Feature-13 section to AGENTS.md with migration learnings and compatibility decisions
Update planning/current-feature.json to track Feature-13 while active
Append implementation notes and reusable patterns to planning/progress.txt

high: Hard renaming module files without shims will break existing user scripts and tests importing cryptoAccounts
Default path migration may lead users to think historical SQLite data is missing if fallback is not explicit
Entry point migration can break packaging if console scripts and module list are not coordinated
Public launch timing increases impact of breaking changes if rebrand lands without a compatibility period
medium: Broad import churn across tests and scripts can hide regressions in less-used workflows
User-facing copy changes may invalidate brittle string-based TUI tests
low: Most rebrand work is deterministic search/replace with controlled compatibility wrappers
Existing test coverage is strong across CLI imports and TUI flows

scope: Remove cryptoAccounts/cryptoAccounting shims after deprecation window
Remove legacy path fallback if desired
followOnFeature.timing: After at least one stable release cycle with deprecation notices and initial public-release feedback

phaseA_private: Ship Feature-13 while repo is private with compatibility shims enabled
Ask current external user to test their existing commands/imports unchanged
phaseB_public: Open repository publicly after Feature-13 docs and migration guidance are merged
Keep legacy aliases active during initial public adoption window
phaseC_cleanup: Execute Feature-14 only after compatibility window and user feedback indicate low risk
